name: es30-vertex-array-objects
title: Vertex array objects, integer and packed attributes
summary: Five VAOs with different buffers, formats, strides and element buffers drawn in alternating order, the VAO name lifecycle, integer attributes (glVertexAttribIPointer / glVertexAttribI4*) proven by values above 2^24, 2_10_10_10 packed and HALF_FLOAT attributes decoded against a CPU model of ES 3.0 equations 2.1/2.2, and the errors the spec defines.
spec: ES 3.0 §2.1.6.1 Conversion from Normalized Fixed-Point to Floating-Point (equations 2.1, 2.2)
ES 3.0 §2.8 Vertex Specification (current generic attribute values, VertexAttribI4*)
ES 3.0 §2.9 Vertex Arrays (Table 2.4, VertexAttribPointer / VertexAttribIPointer, INVALID_OPERATION rules)
ES 3.0 §2.9.3 Drawing Commands (disabled arrays read the current value)
ES 3.0 §2.10.6 Vertex Arrays in Buffer Objects, §2.10.7 Array Indices in Buffer Objects
ES 3.0 Table 6.2 Vertex Array Object State, Table 6.3 Vertex Array Data (not in vertex array objects)
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.3.4 Input Variables, §4.3.6 Output Variables, §4.3.8.1 Input Layout Qualifiers, §4.3.9 Interpolation Qualifiers

api.glGenVertexArrays: 14 VAOs used by the validated draws; a generated but never bound name is not a VAO (glIsVertexArray FALSE)
api.glBindVertexArray: selects all vertex state: A/B/C/D drawn in two different orders match the CPU model; VERTEX_ARRAY_BINDING read back; binding a deleted or never generated name -> INVALID_OPERATION and the binding is unchanged
api.glDeleteVertexArrays: deleting the bound VAO reverts VERTEX_ARRAY_BINDING to 0 and glIsVertexArray to FALSE; deleting a deleted name or 0 raises no error
api.glIsVertexArray: FALSE for 0 and for a generated-but-unbound name, TRUE after the first bind, FALSE after deletion
api.glEnableVertexAttribArray: VERTEX_ATTRIB_ARRAY_ENABLED per VAO read back; index = MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIBS -> INVALID_VALUE
api.glVertexAttribPointer: float, normalized ubyte, normalized short, UNSIGNED_INT_2_10_10_10_REV and INT_2_10_10_10_REV (normalized and not), HALF_FLOAT: all pixels match the CPU conversion; size/type/normalized/stride/pointer/buffer read back; INVALID_OPERATION (non-default VAO + no ARRAY_BUFFER + non-NULL pointer, packed type with size != 4), INVALID_VALUE (size 0/5, negative stride, index)
api.glVertexAttribIPointer: INT, UNSIGNED_INT, SHORT (size 3), UNSIGNED_BYTE (size 2) into ivec4/uvec4: exact integers compared in the shader (values above 2^24); VERTEX_ATTRIB_ARRAY_INTEGER = TRUE; INVALID_ENUM for FLOAT / HALF_FLOAT / packed types, INVALID_OPERATION without ARRAY_BUFFER
api.glVertexAttrib4f: a disabled attribute array supplies the constant color (orange cell matches the model)
api.glVertexAttrib4fv: current attribute value read back exactly with glGetVertexAttribfv
api.glVertexAttribI4i: exact int values (2^24+1, INT_MIN) reach an ivec4 input and read back with glGetVertexAttribIiv; index = MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIBS -> INVALID_VALUE
api.glVertexAttribI4ui: exact uint values (0xFFFFFFFF, 2^24+1) reach a uvec4 input and read back with glGetVertexAttribIuiv
api.glVertexAttribI4iv: int vector reaches the ivec4 input exactly and reads back
api.glVertexAttribI4uiv: uint vector reaches the uvec4 input exactly and reads back
api.glGetVertexAttribiv: ENABLED, SIZE, TYPE, NORMALIZED, STRIDE, INTEGER, DIVISOR, BUFFER_BINDING of 16 attributes in 11 VAOs; initial values of attributes 0, 1, 15 of a fresh VAO
api.glGetVertexAttribfv: CURRENT_VERTEX_ATTRIB after glVertexAttrib4fv, unchanged by a draw that uses an enabled array
api.glGetVertexAttribPointerv: buffer offsets of interleaved attributes; the client pointer of the default VAO
api.glGenBuffers: vertex and index buffers feeding the validated draws
api.glBindBuffer: ARRAY_BUFFER is not VAO state (survives VAO switches, 0 during the draws); ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER is (queried per VAO, edited only in the bound VAO)
api.glBufferData: vertex/index data observed through the rendered pixels
api.glDrawArrays: TRIANGLES and TRIANGLE_STRIP from every VAO kind; pixels match the CPU model
api.glDrawElements: UNSIGNED_SHORT and UNSIGNED_BYTE (byte offset 2) from the element buffer stored in the VAO; the two VAOs sharing a vertex buffer draw different shapes
api.glUseProgram: float and integer programs select the cells
api.glGetUniformLocation: u_scale, u_bias, u_expect_i, u_expect_u located; effects observed in the pixels
api.glUniform4f: u_scale/u_bias map attribute values to colors; the resulting pixels match
api.glUniform4i: u_expect_i: the shader comparison turns red when the value is off by one (negative control)
api.glUniform4ui: u_expect_u compared with the uvec4 input
api.glViewport: per-cell viewports map NDC to the probed pixels
api.glClearColor: background pixels equal the clear color

visual_review.notes: Viewed gpu/llvmpipe/zink captures (256x256; identical within 1/255): top rows show the skewed RGB triangle (A), the yellow/cyan/magenta/white quad (B) and the two bow-tie wedge pairs (C right-left vs D top-bottom) in the order A B C D and again D C B A; row 1 is eight green shades per cell (all 4 integer cells match, 4 columns x ivec4/uvec4 rows with a blue tint in the lower row); bottom row: orange/light-blue UINT_2_10_10_10 quads (left and right half equal), orange/green INT quads (right half has lower alpha), four half-float quads (dark blue, orange, green-cyan, blue) and the orange triangle of VAO E. Background is the dark-blue clear color; no stray marks.
